cohort: The study participants were 54,934 parturients who underwent puerperal perineal tear suturing, with 47 of them requiring re-suturing during their delivery hospitalization.
finding: Early re-suturing of puerperal perineal tears is rare (0.09%) but is associated with increased short-term maternal morbidity, with independent risk factors including cephalic malposition and meconium stained amniotic fluid.
